paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: set your focus on JESUS. The writer says He is the apostle and high priest we confess, and that He has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses (Hebrews 3:1, 3). Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's house, but Christ is faithful as the Son over God's house (Hebrews 3:5-6). Moses is a giant in Israel's story, and Jesus is still GREATER, so there's no better place to put your eyes.

Now here's the part I want you to hold onto. The writer says we are His house, "if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast" (Hebrews 3:6). He warns of a "wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God" and says it was unbelief that kept that wilderness generation from entering His rest (Hebrews 3:12, 19). I think he's saying that a hard heart doesn't happen in one big moment. It happens in the small ones, one "just five more minutes" at a time.

So what do you do with a word like "Today"? You listen today, and you don't wait for a better day. The writer says, "exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin's deceitfulness" (Hebrews 3:13). And we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first (Hebrews 3:14). Keep your eyes on Jesus, keep your friends close, and keep your heart soft. That's a good batch, baker.
